# Temple Scroll Column 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 12 | **Condition:** heavily damaged / fragmentary

---

**12:1** [...] and on the tenth day of this seventh month [...]

**12:2** [...] a holy convocation shall be for you [...]

**12:3** [...] and you shall afflict your souls [...]

**12:4** [...] all work you shall not do [...]

**12:5** [...] for it is a day of atonement, to make atonement for you before Me [...]

**12:6** [...] for every soul that does not afflict itself on this very day [...]

**12:7** [...] shall be cut off from its people [...]

**12:8** [...] and you shall bring near a burnt offering to the LORD, a fire offering of soothing aroma [...]

**12:9** [...] one young bull, son of the herd, one ram [...]

**12:10** [...] seven lambs, sons of a year, without blemish [...]

**12:11** [...] and their grain offering: fine flour mixed with oil, three-tenths for the bull [...]

**12:12** [...] two-tenths for the one ram, one-tenth for each lamb of the seven lambs [...]

**12:13** [...] and one male goat for a sin offering, besides the sin offering of the atonements [...]

**12:14** [...] and the perpetual burnt offering, its grain offering, and their drink offerings [...]

**12:15** [...] according to their ordinance, a fire offering of soothing aroma to the LORD [...]

**12:16** [...] a statute forever in all your dwelling places [...]

---

*EMET notes: Column 12 is heavily damaged. Content parallels Numbers 29:7-11 and Leviticus 16, prescribing the Day of Atonement (yom ha-kippurim) in divine first-person. "Afflict your souls" (ve-innitem et nafshoteikhem) preserved literally — the traditional self-denial formula. "Sin offering of the atonements" distinguishes the special Yom Kippur chattat from the standard sin offering. The karet penalty ("cut off") is explicitly stated for non-observance.*
